children: will increase prices of select models and variants by up to 8,000 rupees ($86.10), while Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles
will increase prices of its cars and SUVs by an average of 0.5%, the automakers said on Tuesday.
The price hikes, set to go into effect from December 1, are aimed at partly offsetting a sharp increase in input costs.
Tata said the hike would be applicable across its entire portfolio of internal combustion engine and electric vehicles, but that the extent would vary depending on the model and variant
Automakers in India have been battling higher raw material costs, particularly for steel and copper
Supply-chain disruptions linked to the prolonged Middle East conflict have also added pressure on margins, prompting several manufacturers to raise vehicle prices
Hyundai said it had absorbed a substantial portion of the cost inflation through internal efficiency gains and cost-optimisation measures
Hyundai India's and Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles' price hikes come after market leader Maruti Suzuki
said on Sunday that it would hike prices on select models due to rising commodity costs.
